nodes.label: Collaborative editing for markdown notes
nodes.description: Plan root. Read order: **Requirements** first, then every decision links back to the requirement it serves (`because`), every rejected alternative links to the decision that beat it (`rejects`).

nodes.label: Several people edit one note live
nodes.description: Up to **~10 concurrent editors per note** (assumption, see `q-concurrency`). A remote keystroke appears in **under 300 ms p95** within one region. All replicas converge to byte-identical text; no keystroke is silently dropped.

nodes.label: Live cursors and selections
nodes.description: Each collaborator shows a named, colored caret and selection. Movement looks smooth (updates at **~20 Hz**). Cursor data is disposable: never needs to survive a restart.

nodes.label: Works offline, syncs later
nodes.description: Editing continues with no network for **hours to days** (exact bound is `q-offline`). On reconnect, edits made on several devices merge with **no manual conflict dialog** and no lost text.

nodes.label: Notes stay plain markdown
nodes.description: The note remains a markdown string for search, export, the public API and any existing consumers. The collaboration layer must not turn notes into a rich-text tree that cannot round-trip to markdown.

nodes.label: 50k users
nodes.description: Working assumption: **~10% concurrently online at peak = ~5k WebSockets**, **~1k active rooms**, most with 1-3 people. Needs confirmation (`q-concurrency`); every capacity number below inherits this uncertainty.

nodes.label: React, Node, Postgres
nodes.description: Keep the current stack. **No new datastore in v1** (no Redis, no Mongo, no object store) unless a decision below proves it necessary.

nodes.label: Only permitted people join a note
nodes.description: Implied by any notes app. Enforced when the socket opens **and** on every update (read-only members must not be able to write). Revocation takes effect within seconds.

nodes.label: Never lose an acknowledged edit
nodes.description: Implied. An edit the user saw as synced survives a server crash, deploy or Postgres failover. An edit still only on the client stays on the client until acknowledged.

nodes.label: Use Yjs (CRDT) for the document model
nodes.description:
Notes are a single `Y.Text`. Merging is commutative and idempotent, so the **same code path** serves live typing, reconnect after a flaky network and a week-long offline edit. Updates are binary diffs (typically 20-200 bytes per keystroke batch).

Trade-off: the document carries history (tombstones), so it only grows; see `risk-tombstones`.

nodes.label: Build the room server on Hocuspocus
nodes.description:
Hocuspocus (MIT, Node, Yjs-native) already implements the sync protocol, awareness, auth hooks (`onAuthenticate`) and persistence hooks (`onStoreDocument`). Roughly **2-3 weeks saved** over writing it ourselves. We keep Postgres persistence and auth as our own extensions.

Trade-off: dependency on a small project; pin the version and keep the extension surface thin (`risk-dependency`).

nodes.label: One WebSocket per open note, binary y-protocol
nodes.description: Bidirectional, low-latency, binary. Heartbeat 25 s, reconnect with jitter. A browser holds 1-3 sockets (open tabs), not one per user session.

nodes.label: Sticky routing: one process owns a room
nodes.description:
The load balancer hashes `note_id` (consistent hash) so every client of a note lands on the same Node process. That process holds the single in-memory `Y.Doc`, so **no cross-node pub/sub is needed at 50k users**.

If a node dies, its rooms re-hash to others and clients reconnect and resync via state vectors; clients still hold unacknowledged edits.

nodes.label: Keep active docs in memory, flush in batches
nodes.description:
Server keeps the `Y.Doc` while a room has clients; persists at most every **500 ms or 50 updates**, whichever first (debounced append to `note_updates`). Evict the doc **60 s** after the last client leaves.

Why: one insert per keystroke would be ~100 inserts/s per busy room.

nodes.label: Sync server (Node, Hocuspocus)
nodes.description: Stateless-looking, stateful in practice: rooms in memory. Extensions: `AuthExt` (JWT + ACL), `PgPersistExt` (load snapshot + replay updates, append on store), `MaterializeExt` (write markdown column), metrics. Runs as N processes behind `cmp-router`.

nodes.label: Room router (L7 load balancer rule)
nodes.description: nginx/Envoy/ALB rule hashing `/collab/:noteId` to a backend. Health-checked; removing a node triggers re-hash. No custom code if the existing LB supports consistent hashing (`q-hosting`).

nodes.label: OT with ShareDB
nodes.description: Needs a central server that serializes every op, and offline edits for days mean transforming huge backlogs against server history. Rejected because it makes `req-offline` the hardest part instead of a by-product. ShareDB Postgres adapter is also a weaker fit.

nodes.label: Automerge
nodes.description: Good CRDT, but heavier on documents with long text histories and a less mature CodeMirror binding at the time of writing. Yjs has the larger ecosystem for exactly this stack (editor bindings, awareness, persistence providers).

nodes.label: Last-write-wins on the whole note
nodes.description: Simplest. Loses concurrent edits by design, which violates `req-durable` and makes offline sync destructive. Rejected.

nodes.label: SSE + POST instead of WebSocket
nodes.description: Works through every proxy, but cursors at 20 Hz mean many small POSTs and no server-initiated binary stream; head-of-line behavior is worse. Kept only as a possible fallback transport, not in v1.

nodes.label: Redis pub/sub between nodes
nodes.description: Needed only if one note could be served by several nodes. Sticky routing avoids that; Redis adds a new stateful dependency and failure mode, against `req-stack`. Revisit if routing proves unreliable or rooms exceed one node.

nodes.label: Write the sync server from scratch
nodes.description: Full control, but re-implements a protocol that is easy to get subtly wrong (state-vector handshake, awareness expiry). Not where our differentiation is.

nodes.label: Hosted sync (Liveblocks, Y-Sweet cloud)
nodes.description: Fastest start, but note content leaves our infrastructure and cost scales per MAU/connection; at 50k users likely higher than running 3 Node processes. Reopen if data residency is not a concern (`q-hosting`).

nodes.label: Concurrent edits can yield odd markdown
nodes.description: Two people editing the same table row or list item merge character-wise: the text is convergent but may be syntactically broken (half a row, doubled list marker). Not data loss, but looks like a bug.

nodes.label: Hocuspocus is a small-project dependency
nodes.description:
Maintainer risk and breaking changes between majors. Mitigation: pin, wrap behind our own `RoomServer` interface, keep a fork-ready test suite.

**Review change:** add an exit plan: the `RoomServer` wrapper is ~300 lines, and `y-websocket` is the fallback with the same Yjs protocol.

nodes.label: Node crash loses up to 500 ms of unflushed server state
nodes.description: Updates acknowledged to a client but not yet in Postgres. Clients keep their local copy (IndexedDB) and resend the diff via state vector, so loss happens only if the client is also gone.

nodes.label: CodeMirror 6 with y-codemirror.next, markdown as source
nodes.description:
Edit the markdown **source** (syntax highlighted), bind `Y.Text` directly with `y-codemirror.next`, which also renders remote cursors and per-user undo. The existing preview pane stays a separate render.

Keeps `req-markdown` trivially true: the CRDT value *is* the markdown string.

nodes.label: Cursors via Yjs awareness, ephemeral
nodes.description: Awareness state `{user, color, anchor, head}`; coalesce to one message per **50 ms**; expire after 30 s without heartbeat. Never written to Postgres. Cap on 50 visible cursors per note, rest collapsed into an avatar count.

nodes.label: Sanitized preview of the shared text
nodes.description: Preview is rendered with markdown-it + DOMPurify. Because other users now control the text you render, treat all content as untrusted.

nodes.label: Editor component (React)
nodes.description: `<NoteEditor noteId>` owns the `Y.Doc`, the provider and the CodeMirror view. Mounting/unmounting must destroy provider and awareness (React StrictMode double-mount is a known leak source).

nodes.label: Sync client (provider)
nodes.description: Wraps `HocuspocusProvider` + `y-indexeddb`. Exposes status: `offline | connecting | synced | unsynced-local-edits` for the UI.

nodes.label: Cursor and presence UI
nodes.description: Colored carets, name flags, avatar stack in the toolbar. Colors derived from a hash of user id to stay stable across sessions.

nodes.label: ProseMirror/Tiptap WYSIWYG
nodes.description: Good collaborative support (y-prosemirror), but the document becomes a tree; round-tripping to exact markdown loses formatting choices and breaks `req-markdown` for existing notes. Revisit only if product wants a rich-text mode.

nodes.label: Collaborator-supplied markdown renders in your browser
nodes.description: Before this feature you only rendered your own text. Now an invited user can inject HTML/links/images. Without sanitizing this is stored XSS across accounts.

nodes.label: Undo semantics surprise users
nodes.description: Yjs `UndoManager` undoes only your own edits, which is right, but users used to a global undo may expect otherwise. Needs a UX note, not a design change.

nodes.label: Persist each opened note in IndexedDB (y-indexeddb)
nodes.description: Every edit is written locally before it is sent. Service worker caches the app shell so the app opens offline. Local copy is the safety net behind `req-durable` on the client side.

nodes.label: Resync by state-vector diff
nodes.description: On reconnect the client sends its state vector; the server replies with only what is missing and vice versa. Backoff 1 s to 30 s with jitter to avoid a thundering herd after a deploy (5k clients reconnecting).

nodes.label: Offline for opened and pinned notes only
nodes.description: Cache the last **50 opened notes** plus pinned ones, not the whole library. Bounds IndexedDB use (~50 KB-1 MB each) and avoids a bulk-download sync problem.

nodes.label: Service worker (app shell)
nodes.description: Workbox precache of the JS bundle and routes. Without it the app cannot even start offline, so IndexedDB data would be unreachable.

nodes.label: Local persistence (IndexedDB)
nodes.description: One database per note id; garbage-collected by LRU beyond 50 notes.

nodes.label: Browsers can evict local data
nodes.description:
Safari deletes script-writable storage after ~7 days without interaction; any browser may evict under storage pressure. Offline edits that were never synced could vanish.

**Review change:** mitigated, not just noted. Call `navigator.storage.persist()` on first offline use; the sync indicator shows "N edits only on this device"; after 5 days offline show a banner prompting to reconnect; safe default is that **the server copy is the source of truth**.

nodes.label: Long-offline replicas produce large merges
nodes.description: A device offline for a week while others rewrote the note merges cleanly in the CRDT but may surprise the user. Needs a visible "merged N changes from others" notice.

nodes.label: Append-only update log plus snapshots in Postgres
nodes.description: `note_updates(id bigserial, note_id, update bytea, created_at)` and `note_snapshots(note_id pk, snapshot bytea, upto_update_id)`. Load = snapshot + updates after `upto_update_id`. Index `(note_id, id)`. Binary Yjs updates are the source of truth for collaboration.

nodes.label: Compact log into snapshot
nodes.description:
Background job merges updates into a new snapshot when a note has **>200 updates, >1 MB of log, or 5 min idle**; then deletes merged rows. Keeps load time under ~50 ms and storage near the live document size.

**Review change:** snapshot + delete are one transaction bounded by `upto_update_id`; appends never block on it. Test with a concurrent-append property test.

nodes.label: Materialize markdown text on flush
nodes.description:
On every store (debounced **5 s**) write `Y.Text.toString()` into the existing `notes.markdown` column. Search, export and the public API keep working unchanged. The column is derived: never edited directly while collaboration is on.

**Review change:** search may lag the editor by up to 5 s plus index latency. Acceptable only if `q-existing` shows nothing depends on instant consistency (for example, "save then export").

nodes.label: Postgres tables
nodes.description: `note_updates`, `note_snapshots`, existing `notes`. Partition `note_updates` by hash(note_id) only if the table exceeds ~100 M rows (not expected after compaction).

nodes.label: Compaction worker
nodes.description: Node cron worker, one pass per minute over notes with a dirty counter. Runs outside the room servers to keep their latency flat.

nodes.label: Store documents in object storage or a document DB
nodes.description: S3/Mongo would hold blobs well, but adds a datastore (violates `req-stack`) and loses transactional consistency with `notes` metadata. Postgres `bytea` at <1 MB per doc is fine.

nodes.label: Update log grows without bound if compaction lags
nodes.description: A busy note makes thousands of rows an hour. If compaction stalls, load time and storage degrade silently.

nodes.label: CRDT history only grows
nodes.description: Deleted text stays as tombstones. Typical overhead 2-10x the visible text for heavily edited notes. Yjs garbage collection helps but cannot drop history that peers may still reference.

nodes.label: Write amplification on Postgres
nodes.description: ~1k active rooms x ~1 batched write/s = **~1k inserts/s**, plus materialization (every 5 s per room, +200 updates/s). Review: batch inserts per node per 100 ms (multi-row `INSERT`), keep `note_updates` unlogged-free but with `synchronous_commit=on` only for the flush, not materialization. One primary handles this; replicas are for reads only.

nodes.label: Hard limits per note
nodes.description: Max **1 MB** markdown, **50 editors**, **10 notes** per connection. Beyond the limit the note opens read-only with an explanation. Protects server memory.

nodes.label: Start with 3 sync nodes, scale on sockets
nodes.description: Starting guess: 3 x (2 vCPU, 4 GB), ~4k sockets and ~400 live docs each. **Review:** the memory side was optimistic: with docs at ~8x text size, set `--max-old-space-size` to 3 GB, cap live docs per node at **250**, and evict least-recently-active first. Real numbers come from `task-spike`, not this table. Autoscale on sockets and event-loop lag.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.description: Prometheus metrics: open sockets, rooms, update bytes/s, flush latency, compaction backlog, resync duration; alert on backlog >1000 rows for 10 min and flush p95 >1 s.

nodes.label: In-memory docs can exhaust node memory
nodes.description:
A `Y.Doc` costs several times its text size. 400 docs x 1 MB x ~8 = 3 GB worst case, close to the 4 GB node. Eviction and `dec-limits` bound it, but a hot-note stampede could still OOM.

**Review change:** live-doc cap of 250/node and LRU eviction added to the mitigations.

nodes.label: Deploy or node loss reconnects thousands at once
nodes.description: 5k clients reconnect and request full resync in seconds. Mitigated by jittered backoff and rolling deploys that drain 10% at a time.

nodes.label: Short-lived JWT at upgrade, ACL check, close on revoke
nodes.description: Client gets a 5-minute collab token from the existing API; server verifies it in `onAuthenticate`, loads the note ACL (owner/editor/viewer), and keeps `readOnly` per connection. ACL changes emit `pg_notify("acl", note_id)`; the owning node closes affected sockets.

nodes.label: Auth extension
nodes.description: Hocuspocus extension: verify token, check ACL cache (TTL 10 s), set connection mode.

nodes.label: Removed users keep a live socket
nodes.description: Between ACL change and socket close, up to the notify latency (~seconds) they still receive updates. Acceptable only if stated; tighten with the notify-based close.

nodes.label: Lazy-import existing notes on first collaborative open
nodes.description: If a note has no snapshot, create a `Y.Doc` from `notes.markdown` and persist as snapshot #1 inside a transaction guarded by a unique constraint. No bulk migration, no downtime. Rollback = ignore the collab tables, `notes.markdown` stays current.

nodes.label: Feature-flagged rollout with a read-only kill switch
nodes.description:
Internal team, then 5%, 50%, 100% of notes. Kill switch makes collaboration read-only and falls back to the legacy single-writer save path.

**Review change:** rollout is gated on three green checks: convergence suite, viewer write-rejection test, full 10k-socket load test.

nodes.label: Spike: two tabs, Yjs, CM6, Hocuspocus, Postgres
nodes.description: ~1 week. Proves binding, persistence round trip, **and a 2k-socket k6 test plus a memory profile of 250 live docs** *before* committing to the rest. Output: go/no-go and measured numbers replacing the guesses in `dec-capacity`. If flush p95 >1 s at 2k sockets, stop and revisit `rej-redis` / sharding.

nodes.label: Create tables and persistence extension
nodes.description: Migrations, `PgPersistExt`, load/replay, tests with 10k updates.

nodes.label: Sync server with auth and limits
nodes.description: Hocuspocus app, auth extension, `dec-limits`, health checks, graceful drain.

nodes.label: React editor integration
nodes.description: `NoteEditor`, status indicator, sanitized preview, StrictMode safe teardown.

nodes.label: Cursor UI
nodes.description: Awareness rendering, colors, avatar stack, 50 ms coalescing.

nodes.label: Offline: IndexedDB, service worker, resync
nodes.description: y-indexeddb, Workbox shell, reconnect backoff, "unsynced edits" indicator, test with network throttling and airplane mode.

nodes.label: Compaction worker
nodes.description: Cron worker, dirty counters, backlog metric.

nodes.label: Convergence and chaos tests
nodes.description: fast-check property tests (random ops from N replicas converge) plus toxiproxy-style network cuts during live sessions.

nodes.label: Full load test
nodes.description: k6 websocket scenario: 10k sockets, 1.5k rooms, 20 Hz awareness. Pass: flush p95 <1 s, no node above 70% memory.

nodes.label: Lazy migration path
nodes.description: Implements `dec-migrate`, including race test of two simultaneous first opens.

nodes.label: Rollout and kill switch
nodes.description: Flag plumbing, dashboards, runbook.

nodes.label: Metrics and alerts
nodes.description: Implements `cmp-metrics`.

nodes.label: How are notes stored and consumed today?
nodes.description: Is `notes.markdown` a plain column? Who reads it (search index, export, API, mobile apps)? Decides whether `dec-materialize` is enough or a search reindex hook is needed.

nodes.label: What are real peak concurrent users and editors per note?
nodes.description: Is "50k" registered, monthly or concurrent? Can I see peak concurrent sessions and the largest note? The capacity plan stands on this.

nodes.label: How long must offline editing be supported?
nodes.description: A flight (hours) or weeks? Mobile PWA, or only desktop browsers? Safari eviction (7 days) makes this a real constraint.

nodes.label: Where does it run, and is a hosted sync service acceptable?
nodes.description: Kubernetes or VMs? Does the load balancer support consistent hashing by path? Is there already a Redis? Can note content leave your infrastructure?

nodes.label: What sharing model exists?
nodes.description: Owner/editor/viewer only, link sharing, organizations? Defines the ACL cache and revocation logic.

nodes.label: Is version history or restore needed in v1?
nodes.description: I assume **not in v1**. Review: this is now an explicit non-goal; `dec-erase` and compaction both discard history, so adding version history later needs periodic named snapshots stored separately.

nodes.label: Must deleted text be truly erasable?
nodes.description: GDPR or customer contracts may require that deleted content is gone, but a CRDT keeps it as history. Answer decides whether we need a history-purging path.

nodes.label: Postgres lease per room for single ownership
nodes.description: Review: removed as a decision. For a CRDT a double-hosted room is a **liveness** problem (two halves cannot see each other live), not a **safety** one: both nodes append idempotent updates and the doc converges after reconnect. A lease adds a 5 s heartbeat write per room (~200 writes/s at 1k rooms) and a new failure mode for no correctness gain.

nodes.label: Brief double-hosting of a room during rebalance
nodes.description: Two nodes may host one note for seconds while the LB re-hashes: collaborators temporarily do not see each other. No data loss (idempotent merge). Mitigation: drain on re-hash (close sockets of moved rooms, clients reconnect to the new owner), alert when a note has clients on two nodes.

nodes.label: Read-only members can still send updates
nodes.description: Review gap: authorization at connect is not enough. A viewer's client speaks the same protocol and could push a sync update. Must be dropped server side per message, not hidden in the UI.

nodes.label: Enforce read-only on the server per connection
nodes.description: Hocuspocus `connection.readOnly = true` for viewers: the server applies no incoming update messages from them (awareness still allowed). Test: a viewer socket sending a crafted update leaves the doc and Postgres unchanged.

nodes.label: Viewer write-rejection test
nodes.description: Integration test with a raw WebSocket client sending a crafted update as a viewer; part of the rollout gate.

nodes.label: Compaction can race with live appends
nodes.description: Review gap: if the worker snapshots at update 500 while the server appends 501-503, deleting by note_id would lose them. Safe rule: snapshot records `upto_update_id` and the delete is `WHERE id <= upto_update_id`, in one transaction that also locks the note row (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`).

nodes.label: Erasure = rebuild the doc without history
nodes.description: If `q-erasure` says yes: an admin action creates a fresh `Y.Doc` from the current text, writes it as snapshot, deletes all `note_updates` and forces every client to reload (their old IndexedDB copy is discarded by a doc-epoch counter). Cost: version history and in-flight offline edits of that note are lost, stated in the UI.

nodes.label: Sync status indicator
nodes.description: Review addition. Always-visible state from `cmp-provider`: synced / offline (N local edits) / reconnecting. Makes the offline risk visible to users instead of silent.
